title: Annotatio V §.III open: Lutherans admit double food/eating — yet extend corporal beyond its sphere
pass_a_gloss: §. III. Although indeed Luther and whoever desire to be named from Luther deny to no one both a merely double food in the Sacred Supper and, on account of this double food, a double Eating set forth — corporal of the bread, and spiritual of Christ’s Body — yet, about to extend the Corporal beyond the sphere of its adequate object, namely corporal food, from this, that they conceive too grossly that besides corporal eating no true eating can be given, they invent a double Corporal Eating — one of bread, the other of Christ’s Body.
pass_b_english: §.III: Luther and his namesakes grant a double Supper-food and a double eating — corporal of bread, spiritual of Christ’s Body.

Yet because they grossly hold that nothing but corporal eating is true, they stretch the corporal beyond corporal food’s proper sphere and invent a double corporal eating: one of bread, one of Christ’s Body.
source_text: §. III. Etsi verò Lutherus & quotquot à Luthero denominari gestiunt, cum, duplicem duntaxat in S. Cœna cibum, tùm, ob duplicem hunc cibum, duplicem expositam Manducationem, corporalem panis, & spiritualem Corporis Christi, nulli diffitentur; tamen Corporalem extra objecti sui adæquati, corporalis scil. cibi sphæram, inde extensuri, quod præter corporalem manducationem, veram nullam dari posse, nimis crasse concipiunt, duplicem Corporalem comminiscuntur Manducationem, panis unam, alteram Corporis Christi.
